decisions.statement: A presented secret is matched by its hash rather than by itself.
A page is asked for under the key the page carries rather than under its slug.
The pages are asked of the pages system service rather than opened.
The rows the service answers with are narrowed again here.
Pages that went unread are told apart from pages that matched nothing.
A hash on two pages is read to neither page.
Two hashes are compared in time that does not vary with how the two hashes differ.
A secret is minted only for an account a person states.
A device minting again keeps the page the device is already on.
A page is written as values handed to the pages system service.
Nothing here spells where a device secret page sits.
A page being created takes its identity from the pages system service.
A page written over names the commit that page was read at.
A minting that does not land answers why rather than a secret.
A revoked secret keeps its page rather than losing that page.
No refusal has the secret that was presented.
Nothing here decides an account's reach.
When a secret was last presented is written nowhere.

definition: the account a device presenting a secret represents, and how that secret is kept
